name: Minaprine
summary: Minaprine, sold under the brand name Cantor among others, is a monoamine oxidase inhibitor antidepressant drug that was used in France for the treatment of depression until it was withdrawn from the market in 1996 because it caused convulsions.

pharmacology.text: Minaprine is a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI). A study found that it acts as a reversible inhibitor of MAO-A (RIMA) in rats, albeit with very low potency. In addition to its RIMA activity, minaprine has been found to act as a weak antagonist of the serotonin 5-HT2B receptor (Ki = 863 nM).
pharmacology.kind: Monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI); Reversible inhibitor of MAO-A (RIMA)
